text: Following Carnap, Hirsch and Thomasson defend ___ about ontology: the view that ontological disputes are not deep factual questions about mind-independent reality but turn on the choice of framework or language.
explanation: Deflationism (ontological anti-realism), defended by Carnap, Hirsch, and Thomasson, treats hard ontological questions as trivial, verbal, or framework-relative. It opposes the heavyweight realism of Sider, Schaffer, and Fine, who hold that ontology tracks mind-independent structure.
